title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Deck and fence maintenance
audience: Deck and fence maintenance operators who inspect, clean, re-seal, repair and board-replace timber decks and fences for homeowners, body corporates and rental managers.
learningOutcomes: Write a maintenance offer that starts with an inspection and an itemised written report
Show the scope, exclusions and variation terms that protect the price
Price the offer from value and cost, and compare it with published vendor ranges

instruction.heading: Sell a sound deck or fence for the next season
instruction.body: A deck or fence customer buys a structure they can use safely and a clear view of what it needs. A good first offer is an inspection with an itemised written report, followed by a choice of what to do. A Victorian vendor listing gives a structural inspection and quote at $250 to $600 (The Quote Yard, Victoria, published 2 May 2026). That is a vendor estimate. Use it as a market check and set your own price from your own cost.

instruction.heading: Use three levels that each add something visible
instruction.body: Good could be an inspection and itemised quote. Better could add a clean, a seal and minor repairs such as loose fixings and rails. Best could add a strip and refinish, or a board renewal on a stated area under a written quote. Vendor ranges for Victoria give a deck strip and refinish at $1,500 to $4,500 per job, and full board renewal of a 20 square metre deck at $1,800 to $5,500 per job (The Quote Yard, 2 May 2026). Set your own levels and prices from your cost, and use the vendor ranges as a check.

instruction.heading: Itemise the scope and state the exclusions
instruction.body: Itemise boards, joists, bearers and posts as separate lines, because the vendor listing prices them separately and the customer can see what is included. Exclude rot found after the boards are lifted, unless the variation is approved in writing before the work. The vendor page advises an itemised written quote every time. Exclude council permit fees and approvals unless you have quoted them.

instruction.heading: Variations, contracts and consumer rules
instruction.body: Extra work needs the customer's permission first, and a written quote binds once accepted. Victoria requires a written major domestic building contract for work over $10,000, and that page says the threshold has applied since 1 August 2017. Check that it is still current. Victoria's home-warranty insurance threshold is unresolved, so do not quote a figure for it. New South Wales requires variations to be in writing and signed by both parties for residential contract work.

instruction.heading: Guarantees you can keep
instruction.body: Services must be done with due care and skill, and a business should get a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault. A fix-first window that you set in the offer is a promise you can keep. Do not promise a structural result you cannot measure, and do not promise to make a deck safe for a load it was not designed to carry.

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence a customer would repeat, such as 'the deck is safe to use and sealed for the coming season'.
Offer the inspection and an itemised report, and set the report's delivery date.
Set the three levels of work and list each one's tasks, exclusions and fix-first window.
Itemise the boards, joists, bearers, posts and fixings as separate lines, and state what is excluded.
Price from your cost, check the result against the vendor ranges for the same work, and state GST status.
Confirm the offer in writing, and record any variation approved before the work starts.

workedExamples.situation: A strata manager asks for a quote on a common-area timber deck of about 20 square metres. Some boards look grey and a rail moves when pushed. The scenario is illustrative.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What package should the operator offer, and what must the quote exclude?
workedExamples.reasoning: The condition of the boards is unknown until the deck is inspected, so the operator offers a Better package: an inspection, a clean, fixings and rail repair, and a board renewal priced separately under a written quote after the inspection. Vendor estimates for Victoria are a full board renewal of a 20 square metre deck at $1,800 to $5,500, board supply of treated pine at $25 to $50 per square metre, and a structural inspection at $250 to $600 (The Quote Yard, 2 May 2026). These are vendor estimates and are not used as the price. The quote excludes rot found under the boards, council permit fees and approvals, and any structural repair, which is quoted separately if needed. The threshold for a written major contract in Victoria, and the home-warranty figure, must be checked before the quote is issued, because the Victorian home-warranty figure is unresolved.

equipmentAndPpe: Itemised quote template with boards, joists, bearers, posts and fixings as separate lines
Inspection checklist with photo record of each area
Quote sheet showing GST status and a validity date
PPE as set by the site's own rules and {{business:safety.required_ppe}}

commonErrors.error: Quoting a whole deck as one lump sum with no itemised lines
commonErrors.prevention: Itemise each component and state what is excluded.

commonErrors.error: Starting rot or joist repair without a written variation
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, photograph, price the variation, and get written approval before continuing.

commonErrors.error: Promising a structural result you cannot measure
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the guarantee to a stated fix-first window for minor defects in the work you did.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. The ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited. Show one total with GST status. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority.

Queensland: building work above $3,300 including materials, labour and GST needs a licence. Decks and verandahs also need home-warranty cover when the project cost is more than $3,300 including GST. Fences do not need that cover when done on their own.

Victoria: the home-warranty insurance threshold is unresolved. One Consumer Victoria page says domestic building insurance is needed for works over $16,000, and another says that from 1 July 2026 Home Warranty insurance applies to work worth more than $20,000. Do not state either figure as settled. Check with the Building and Plumbing Commission before quoting.

Council permits: Boroondara says a building permit is always needed to build a deck, and a planning permit may apply in some residential zones. Monash says a building permit may be needed where a deck is attached to a building, is larger than 10 square metres, or is at the front of the property. Check each council for each job.

qualityStandard: Every offer starts with an inspection and an itemised written report.
Every variation is priced and approved in writing before the work starts.
Every quote shows one total with GST status, a validity date and the permit and exclusion notes.
documentationEvidence: Itemised quote with scope, exclusions and validity
Written variation records with the date of approval
summary: Sell an inspection and an itemised report first, then the work the customer chooses.
Itemise the components and state the exclusions and permit position.
Check each Victorian threshold with the regulator, because the home-warranty figure is unresolved.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a maintenance offer does the customer buy?
options: Your hourly rate on its own
A sound deck or fence for the coming season, with a clear view of what it needs
The number of years you have worked on decks

knowledgeChecks.question: A joist turns out to be rotten after the boards are lifted. What must happen before the work continues?
options: Carry on and invoice the extra work later
Stop, photograph the problem, and price the variation for written approval
Replace the joist without telling the customer
Ask the neighbour whether the customer wants it fixed

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a guarantee in a deck maintenance offer be?
options: A structural result you cannot measure
A fix-first window for minor defects in your own work, set in the offer
Available only if the customer never uses the deck

business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', https://business.gov.au/people/contractors/prepare-quotes, last updated 1 August 2025. A written quote becomes binding once accepted.

Consumer Victoria, 'Services not done with due care and skill', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/products-and-services/problem-with-a-service/services-not-done-with-due-care-and-skill, last updated 13 October 2023. Due care and skill; a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault.

Consumer Victoria, 'What work requires a building contract', https://cms9.consumer.vic.gov.au/licensing-and-registration/builders-and-tradespeople/running-your-business/domestic-building-contracts/what-work-requires-a-building-contract, threshold shown as 'From 1 August 2017'. Written contract for work over $10,000; landscaping, driveways and fencing listed as covered work in home construction.

Consumer Victoria, 'Domestic building insurance', https://consumer.vic.gov.au/licensing-and-registration/builders-and-tradespeople/running-your-business/warranties-and-insurance/domestic-building-insurance, last updated 2 October 2026. States $16,000; conflicts with the $20,000 figure from 1 July 2026, unresolved.

Consumer Victoria, 'Insurance and insolvency', https://consumer.vic.gov.au/housing/building-and-renovating/defects-delays-and-insolvency/insurance-and-insolvency, no date shown. States $20,000 from 1 July 2026; conflicts with the $16,000 figure, unresolved.

Queensland Building and Construction Commission, 'Home warranty cover', https://www.qbcc.qld.gov.au/node/2886, last reviewed 1 August 2024. Decks and verandahs above $3,300 including GST; fences do not need cover on their own.

Boroondara City Council, 'Deck permits', https://www.boroondara.vic.gov.au/planning-building/do-i-need-permit/deck-permits, last modified 11 August 2026. A building permit is always needed to build a deck.
Monash City Council, 'Decks', https://www.monash.vic.gov.au/Planning-Development/Building/Do-I-Need-a-Building-Permit/Decks, no date shown. A building permit may be required in the stated cases.
